latest_release.body:
## What's New
- **iOS:** Add `onScaleChange` support to report zoom scale changes continuously during pinch gestures and zoom animations (#72 by @LuizAbudi).
- **Android & iOS:** Add imperative `scrollToIndex(index)` ref method (`PdfRendererViewRefType`) to programmatically jump to a page and reset zoom (#81 by @LuizAbudi).
- **Android & iOS:** Add `initialPageIndex` prop to open a document directly on a specific zero-based page without a visual jump (#81 by @LuizAbudi).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/douglasjunior/react-native-pdf-renderer/compare/3.0.1...3.1.0

detail.readme:
A zoomable, blazing fast, zero dependencies, pure native, typed PDF Renderer for Android and iOS.

React Native PDF Renderer provides high-performance, dependency-free native PDF rendering for React Native by directly utilizing Android's PdfRenderer and Apple's PDFKit. Enjoy smooth multi-page scrolling, fluid pinch-to-zoom, thumbnail previews, and comprehensive scale events without the maintenance burden of third-party native binaries.

Quick Start · Why · Previews · Requirements · Installation · Usage · API Reference · Limitations · Testing · Contributing

--- ## 🚀 Quick Start ```bash # 1. Install package yarn add react-native-pdf-renderer # or: npm i -S react-native-pdf-renderer # 2. Install CocoaPods dependencies for iOS cd ios && pod install ``` ```tsx import React from 'react'; import { SafeAreaView } from 'react-native-safe-area-context'; import PdfRendererView from 'react-native-pdf-renderer'; export default function App() { return ( { console.log(`Page: ${current + 1} of ${total}`); }} /> ); } ``` --- ## 💡 Why Another PDF Renderer? The main reason why this library was created is to **avoid using third-party native dependencies**, such as `com.github.TalbotGooday:AndroidPdfViewer`, `com.github.mhiew:android-pdf-viewer`, `react-native-blob-util`, or `react-native-webview`. ### But why? Every React Native developer knows (or will discover soon) [the pain of updating the React Native ecosystem](https://x.com/flexbox_/status/1806786055057674337) whenever a new major Android or iOS version comes out. Third-party native wrappers often become abandoned, break during Gradle or Xcode updates, or introduce incompatible native architectures. Here, we eliminate this friction entirely: - ⚛️ **Pure Platform Native:** Relies exclusively on official platform SDK engines: [PdfRenderer](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/graphics/pdf/PdfRenderer) on Android and [PDFKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/pdfkit) on iOS. - 🛡️ **Zero Native Bloat:** Zero third-party C++/Java/Obj-C dependencies to link, compile, or debug during React Native upgrades. - 🔍 **Pinch-to-Zoom & Pan:** Smooth, continuous gesture-based scaling with configurable zoom ceilings and scale tracking. - 📑 **Single & Multi-Page Modes:** Seamless vertical continuous scroll for multi-page documents, or single-page view for thumbnail covers. - 🛡️ **OOM & Canvas Crash Prevention:** Built-in `maxPageResolution` safeguards on Android prevent out-of-memory bitmap allocations during deep zooms. - 📘 **TypeScript Included:** Written in TypeScript with complete prop definitions and IntelliSense documentation. - 🧪 **Mock Ready:** Pre-configured Jest mock included for painless snapshot and unit testing. --- ## 📸 Previews | Android | iOS | |:---:|:---:| | | | --- ## 📋 Requirements | Platform / Tool | Minimum Version | Notes | |---|---|---| | **React Native** | `>= 0.80.0` | Old & New Architecture support | | **iOS** | `>= 12.0` | Uses native `PDFKit` | | **Android** | `API 21+` (Android 5.0+) | Uses native `android.graphics.pdf.PdfRenderer` | --- ## 📦 Installation ### 1. Install JavaScript Package Using yarn: ```bash yarn add react-native-pdf-renderer ``` Using npm: ```bash npm i -S react-native-pdf-renderer ``` ### 2. iOS CocoaPods Setup Navigate to your `ios` folder and run `pod install`: ```bash cd ios && pod install ``` ### 3. Android Specific Setup (Optional) You can customize the [`androidx.recyclerview:recyclerview`](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/recyclerview) version by configuring `ext` inside your root `android/build.gradle` file (defaults to `1.4.0`): ```gradle buildscript { ext { recyclerViewVersion = "1.4.0" } ... } ``` --- ## 🛠 Basic Usage There is only one primary component that you need to render PDF documents: ``. ```tsx import React from 'react'; import { View, StyleSheet } from 'react-native'; import { SafeAreaView } from 'react-native-safe-area-context'; import PdfRendererView from 'react-native-pdf-renderer'; const App = () => { return ( { console.log(`Current page: ${current + 1} / ${total}`); }} onError={() => { console.warn('Failed to load PDF'); }} /> ); }; const styles = StyleSheet.create({ container: { flex: 1, }, pdf: { flex: 1, backgroundColor: '#1e1e1e', }, }); export default App; ``` ### 📁 Working with Remote Files > [!IMPORTANT] > The `source` prop **must point to a local file stored inside the device's storage** (e.g., `file:///data/user/0/...` or `file:///var/mobile/...`). If your PDF file is hosted on a remote server, download it to device storage first using a file system library such as [`expo-file-system`](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/filesystem/) (use `expo-file-system/legacy` on Expo SDK 54+), `react-native-blob-util`, or `rn-fetch-blob`: ```tsx import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react'; import { ActivityIndicator, StyleSheet, Text, View } from 'react-native'; // Note: expo-file-system/legacy is used on Expo SDK 54+; earlier SDKs import from 'expo-file-system' import * as FileSystem from 'expo-file-system/legacy'; import PdfRendererView from 'react-native-pdf-renderer'; export function RemotePdfViewer({ url }: { url: string }) { const [localUri, setLocalUri] = useState(null); const [error, setError] = useState(null); useEffect(() => { let isMounted = true; async function downloadPdf() { try { setError(null); const fileUri = `${FileSystem.documentDirectory}document.pdf`; const result = await FileSystem.downloadAsync(url, fileUri); if (result.status < 200 || result.status >= 300) { throw new Error(`Download failed (HTTP ${result.status})`); } if (isMounted) { setLocalUri(result.uri); } } catch (err) { if (isMounted) { setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to download PDF'); } } } downloadPdf(); return () => { isMounted = false; }; }, [url]); if (error) { return ( {error} ); } if (!localUri) { return ( ); } return ( ); } const styles = StyleSheet.create({ center: { flex: 1, justifyContent: 'center', alignItems: 'center', }, errorText: { color: '#ef4444', fontSize: 14, }, }); ``` For a comprehensive real-world example featuring scale indicators, full-screen toggles, and modal dialogues, see the [Sample Project](https://github.com/douglasjunior/react-native-pdf-renderer/blob/main/Sample/App.tsx). --- ## 📖 API Reference ### `` Props | Prop | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|:---:|---| | `source` | `string` | — | Path to a local file stored on the device (e.g. `file:///path/to/file.pdf`). | | `initialPageIndex` | `number` | `0` | Zero-based page index shown when the document opens. It is read when `source` changes; changing only `initialPageIndex` does nothing. Changing `singlePage` or `maxZoom` reloads the document, which opens on this page again. Out-of-range values and `singlePage` open the first page. Use `scrollToIndex` to navigate in an already open document. | | `distanceBetweenPages` | `number` | `16` | Vertical spacing in `DPI` between rendered pages. | | `maxZoom` | `number` | `5` | Maximum allowable zoom scale factor. | | `maxPageResolution` | `number` | `2048` | *(Android only)* Maximum page resolution (width/height) in pixels when zooming. Designed to prevent Android OOM / Canvas crashes when zooming deeply ([#26](https://github.com/douglasjunior/react-native-pdf-renderer/issues/26)). | | `singlePage` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders only the first page without scrolling. Ideal for displaying document thumbnails. | | `onPageChange` | `(current: number, total: number) => void` | — | Callback invoked when the user scrolls between pages. `current` is zero-indexed. | | `onScaleChange` | `(scale: number) => void` | — | Invoked when the zoom scale changes: continuously during pinch gestures and on double-tap zoom on both platforms. On iOS, zoom animations can also report intermediate values; on Android, double-tap zoom reports the final value at once. `1` is the unzoomed baseline: fit-to-width in multi-page mode and fit-to-center in single-page mode on Android, or the fitted size provided by PDFKit on iOS. The value never exceeds `maxZoom`. | | `onError` | `() => void` | — | Callback invoked when an error occurs while rendering the PDF. | | `style` | `StyleProp` | — | Styles applied to the native view container. *(Note: border radius is not directly supported; see [Limitations](#border-radius)).* | | `testID` | `string` | — | Optional identifier used to locate this view in automated end-to-end testing. | ### `` Methods Methods are called through a `ref`, typed with `PdfRendererViewRefType`: ```tsx import React, { useRef } from 'react'; import { Button } from 'react-native'; import PdfRendererView, { PdfRendererViewRefType } from 'react-native-pdf-renderer'; const App = () => { const pdfRef = useRef(null); return ( <>
